question: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched according to mode of reproduction?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bryophyllum - Spore formation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bryophyllum** reproduces vegetatively through leaf buds, not through spore formation.
 
• **Vegetative reproduction** in Bryophyllum occurs when plantlets arise from the notches at the margins of its leaves.
 
• Each plantlet can develop into a new individual when it falls onto the soil, a process known as **propagation by fragmentation**.
 
• In contrast, **spore formation** is a mode of asexual reproduction seen in fungi, algae, and some non-flowering plants, but not in Bryophyllum.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Binary Fission in Amoeba**

 
 
• Amoeba reproduces asexually by binary fission, where the cell divides into two equal parts.
 
• This process involves the replication of the genetic material followed by the division of the cytoplasm.
 
 
 
• **Budding in Hydra**
 
 
• Hydra reproduces by budding, a form of asexual reproduction where a new organism develops from an outgrowth or bud on the parent.
 
• The bud detaches when it is mature enough to survive on its own.
 
 
 
• **Fragmentation in Spirogyra**
 
 
• Spirogyra, a filamentous green alga, reproduces through fragmentation where a filament breaks into smaller pieces, each of which can grow into a new individual.
 
• This method is common in simple multicellular organisms and some plants.
